question.problem: Given that $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]$ is a non-zero vector that is orthogonal to the set $W=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\},$ find the value of $\frac{b+c}{a}.$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $u\cdot {w}_{1}=0$ and $u\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:    

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1}=0 \\ u\cdot {w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd), so ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=5{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=1$, we get the vector 
$[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we obtain $a=-2,$ $b=5,$ and $c=1.$

Finally, $\frac{b+c}{a}=\frac{5+1}{-2}=-3.$
